first_impression.reaction: My daughter sent it, so I'll read it properly. The ring is her fiance's business, not mine, but I liked that it isn't gossip. 'This one reads each ring the way a jeweller would' told me it was going to be sensible.

journey.quote: Where outlets disagree on a detail, we have left it out rather than choose between them.
journey.reaction: Good. Somebody is being careful with facts. That's what I want from the people handling my money too.

journey.quote: Mary was born in Hobart, Tasmania.
journey.reaction: Our Mary. Nice to see an Australian touch, I'd mention that to my husband.

journey.quote: The next 14 rings run from the late 2000s to 2025, and several were first seen on Instagram rather than at a palace photocall.
journey.reaction: By here I'm skimming. I don't know half these people and it's a long scroll on the iPad. It's not slangy though, so no harm done.

journey.section: Sun, salt water and long-haul flights
journey.quote: Before you leave, check that the ring is covered by your insurance while travelling overseas, and keep a recent photograph of it with your travel documents. Carry it on your hand or in your cabin bag, never in checked luggage.
journey.reaction: Now that's practical. This is the bit I'll forward to my daughter. Insurance is exactly what I'd ask about.

journey.quote: a Wedded Advisor can plan the venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world, as your single point of contact from the first idea to the last dance.
journey.reaction: One person responsible, and they handle payments. That's what I want to hear. But who is this person, and is the deposit protected? It doesn't say.

unanswered_questions: Who exactly is the Wedded Advisor, and can I speak to them on the phone before anything is booked?
When you say you handle payments, are deposits to overseas suppliers protected, and are fees agreed in writing in Australian dollars?
Who do I ring if something goes wrong at 2am on the other side of the world?
would_share_with: My daughter (the travel and insurance section)
My husband, with a note about the Wedded Advisor

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready to talk it through, [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=internal&utm_campaign=celebrity-engagement-rings) is the place to start.
cta_reaction.why: 'Talk it through' is the right idea, I want a phone call. But I'd only click once my daughter has a destination in mind, and I'd want to know it's a real person and how payments and deposits work before I give anyone our details.

top_3_changes: In the closing section, add one plain line on how payments work: fees agreed in writing, quotes in AUD, and what happens to deposits.
Say that the first step is a phone call with a named Wedded Advisor, so a parent knows there is a person, not a form.
Put the insurance and cabin-bag advice higher or in a short boxed checklist; it's the most useful part for a family reader and it's buried after 25 rings.

Stayed in character as Margaret, funding parent, reading on an iPad from her daughter's link
No invented brand facts; missing details listed as unanswered questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments treated as invisible
No invented problems; turn_offs_found left empty because none of my turn-offs appear
